newsitem.title: USA: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. jobless claims rose in latest week.

text.p: U.S. Labor Department report of initial state jobless benefit claims, seasonally adjusted.
Week Ended Initial Claims 4-Week Avg. Continued Claims
R-Revised, Dec 21 Initial Claims from 335,000; Dec 21 Four-Week Average from 341,250; Dec 14 Continued Claims from 2,457,000 and Dec 7 from 2,490,000.
The department said initial claims of 366,000 in the week ended December 28 were the highest since the July 13 week when they reached 367,000.
The department said 17 states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended December 21, the latest period for which data are available.
Among the largest were Virginia, with 6,661 additional jobless claims, Kentucky with 5,201, Texas with 4,108, Illinois with 4,030, Missouri with 3,341 and Indiana with 3,168.
Virginia reported layoffs in the textile, apparel, food and primary metals industries. Kentucky had layoffs in the glass and electrical equipment industries.
In Illinois and Missouri there were layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries. Missouri also had layoffs in the glass industry and Illinois in manufacturing.

Indiana reported layoffs in the rubber, lumber, transportation equipment, fabricated metals, electrical equipment and non-electrical machinery industries. Texas provided no reason for its increase in claims.
Labor said five states reported decreases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the December 21 week.
They were California, with 10,680 fewer claims filings, North Carolina with 7,003, Georgia with 3,064, South Carolina with 2,649 and Alabama with 1,544.
California said it had fewer layoffs in the construction industry and in agriculture, while North Carolina reported fewer layoffs in the textile, furniture and electrical equipment industries.
Alabama had fewer layoffs in the textile, apparel and service industries. Georgia and South Carolina had no comment.
